title: Canonical Shared Types
description: Canonical definitions for shared logical fields (foreign-key identifiers and timestamps). Reference these instead of re-modeling ids/timestamps ad-hoc per schema, to stop cross-schema drift (#137). ForeignKeyId accepts BOTH server-generated UUID4 ids and SDK-generated trial_<hex> ids (the two real id populations).

ForeignKeyId.description: Canonical foreign-key identifier. NOT format:uuid — accepts UUID4 (server) and trial_<hex>/<optimization_id>_<n> (SDK). A format:uuid constraint on these fields rejects real SDK ids (422).

Priority.description: Canonical categorical priority vocabulary (low < normal < high). Reference this instead of re-spelling the enum per schema (#313); use PriorityWithCritical where a fourth 'critical' tier is offered. Note: 'normal' is the canonical middle rank — schemas that emit 'medium' are drifted spellings of the same tier.

PriorityWithCritical.description: Canonical categorical priority vocabulary with an escalation tier (low < normal < high < critical). Superset of Priority (#313). Distinct from the integer 'priority' rank-order fields, which are numeric ordering, not this severity vocabulary.

CacheReadTokens.description: Canonical count of input tokens served from a provider prompt cache, billed at a discounted cache-read rate. NULLABLE BY DESIGN: null means the provider did not report the field, which is NOT the same as zero. Defaulting a silent provider to 0 makes 'no cache dimension reported' indistinguishable from 'no cache was used' and yields a confidently wrong cost (Amazon Nova omits the keys entirely rather than reporting 0). Consumers that need to know why a count is null read unreported_usage_fields. Normalized from usage.prompt_tokens_details.cached_tokens (OpenAI Chat Completions), usage.input_tokens_details.cached_tokens (OpenAI Responses), usage.cache_read_input_tokens (Anthropic), usage.cacheReadInputTokens (Bedrock Converse), usageMetadata.cachedContentTokenCount (Gemini). NOTE ON DISJOINTNESS: Bedrock reports cache reads DISJOINTLY from inputTokens, while OpenAI reports them as a SUBSET of prompt_tokens — a cost calculation must know which convention produced the numbers, so producers normalize to the disjoint convention (input_tokens excludes cache_read_tokens).

CacheCreationTokens.description: Canonical count of input tokens written into a provider prompt cache, billed at a PREMIUM over fresh input (so cache accounting errors run in both directions and cannot be dismissed as a conservative margin). Nullable with the same absent-is-not-zero semantics as CacheReadTokens. Normalized from usage.cache_creation_input_tokens (Anthropic) and usage.cacheWriteInputTokens (Bedrock Converse); providers with automatic caching (OpenAI, Gemini) do not report a cache-write count and leave this null. CARRIES NO TTL TIER, AND THE PREMIUM DEPENDS ON ONE: Anthropic prices a 5-minute cache write at 1.25x base input and a 1-hour write at 2x. A consumer that multiplies this count by a single configured rate is therefore assuming a tier, and is wrong by 60% on the other one. Until the tier is modelled, a pricing path MUST either know out-of-band which tier it uses or refuse to price the write — it must not silently apply the 5-minute rate, which is the same absent-dimension defect these definitions exist to remove. Spelling note: this is the concept some provider docs call 'cache write'; the name matches the vocabulary already established in harness_session_record.json rather than introducing a third spelling.

UnreportedUsageFields.description: Names of canonical usage fields the provider did not report for this record, e.g. ["cache_read_tokens", "cache_creation_tokens"]. Disambiguates the two reasons a count is null: the provider stayed silent (field listed here) versus the producer never populated the dimension at all (field absent from this list). Without it a null is unattributable, and cost consumers cannot tell a genuine unknown from a producer that predates the field.
